summary: The skill guides an agent through fulfilling a git escrow bounty: it validates an escrow with the git-escrows CLI, clones a test repo, writes or accepts a solution, commits it, and submits it on-chain with `git-escrows fulfill`. It needs the git-escrows and git binaries, a local .env holding PRIVATE_KEY (a wallet key), and network access to an Ethereum RPC endpoint (Sepolia in the example) plus whichever git host serves the test and solution repos. requires.env declares nothing, although PRIVATE_KEY is used as primaryEnv.

findings.message: Compatibility line requires a configured .env with PRIVATE_KEY, so the skill relies on a wallet private key to sign on-chain escrow transactions.
It suggests running `git-escrows new-client --privateKey "0x..."`, which puts a raw private key on the command line and into shell history.
primaryEnv is PRIVATE_KEY, but metadata.openclaw.requires.env declares no environment variables, so the key requirement is undeclared.
The skill depends on an unpinned global npm install of git-escrows (`npm i -g git-escrows`), and line 66 falls back to npx/bunx, which run whatever package version is current.
`git-escrows fulfill` sends a signed transaction to an Ethereum RPC endpoint (Sepolia in the example) that the skill does not name or pin.
It clones an arbitrary test repo URL taken from the escrow into /tmp, fetching untrusted content from whatever git host the escrow names.
The skill card itself acknowledges risks of wallet private key use, secrets pasted into prompts, and an unpinned CLI, while SKILL.md has no explicit user-confirmation step before fulfill or collect.
